# Kyro Wallet

> Kyro Wallet is a free, open-source (GPL-3.0-or-later), non-custodial crypto wallet for Windows, macOS and Linux. Keys are encrypted on the user's computer and every transaction is decoded and confirmed in a system window before signing. Current version: 1.0.7.

Key facts:

- Price: free. Sending, receiving and staking cost only the network fee. Swaps from 0.7%: the Kyro swap fee depends on the swap value (5% for $5 or less, 0.7% from $10,000, 0.9% if the token price is unknown) and is already deducted from the amount received. Providers charge their own costs too: NEAR Intents takes an amount equal to the Kyro fee on the routes it serves directly, so those swaps cost about double the Kyro rate. The quote shown already includes everything. Full table: https://kyrowallet.com/fees/
- Custody: non-custodial. No account, no server holding funds. Standard 12 or 24-word BIP39 recovery phrases.
- Blockchains (36): Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB Chain, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Avalanche, Cronos, Mantle, Sonic, Flare, Kaia, Gnosis, HyperEVM, Sei, Conflux, Solana, TRON, Cardano, XRP Ledger, Litecoin, Dogecoin, Bitcoin Cash, Dash, Stellar, NEAR, Sui, Monero, TON, Cosmos Hub, Polkadot, Aptos, Algorand, Kaspa and Zcash. 220+ tokens.
- Earn: staking for SOL (Solana), ADA (Cardano), TRX (TRON) and NEAR; ETH liquid staking with Lido; lending on Aave v3. 14 options in all. Rates are estimates, never guaranteed, and nothing here is financial advice.
- Hardware wallets: Ledger and Trezor (including Trezor Safe 7) on Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB Chain, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Avalanche, Cronos, Mantle, Sonic, Flare, Kaia, Gnosis, HyperEVM, Sei, Conflux, Solana, TRON, Cardano, XRP Ledger, Litecoin, Dogecoin, Bitcoin Cash, Dash, Stellar, NEAR, Sui, TON, Cosmos Hub, Aptos, Algorand and Zcash. From a hardware account, Earn covers Lido and Aave only.
- Privacy: Tor built in and on by default, no personal data collected (only an anonymous weekly count over Tor, can be turned off), optional custom servers.
- Security status: internal security review done; no external audit published yet. Installers are not code-signed yet, so Windows and macOS warn on first launch.
- Downloads: only from GitHub Releases (https://github.com/shuntraa/kyro-wallet/releases). No mobile app.
- Vulnerability reports: privately via GitHub security advisories (https://github.com/shuntraa/kyro-wallet/security).

## Pages

- [Features](https://kyrowallet.com/features/): What Kyro Wallet does: one portfolio for 36 blockchains, token swaps, staking and lending, Ledger and Trezor, built-in Tor and transactions you can read before you sign.
- [Security](https://kyrowallet.com/security/): Keys encrypted on your device with Argon2id and XChaCha20-Poly1305, signing in a Rust core, a system confirmation window, Tor by default. What Kyro protects against, what it cannot, and its audit status.
- [Fees](https://kyrowallet.com/fees/): Kyro Wallet is free. Sending, receiving and staking cost only the network fee. Swaps carry a Kyro fee from 0.7% to 5% depending on the swap value, plus the provider's own costs, all already included in the quote.
- [Download](https://kyrowallet.com/download/): Install Kyro Wallet 1.0.7 with one command on Windows, macOS or Linux, or download the .exe, .msi, .dmg, AppImage or .deb. How to check the SHA-256 checksum.
- [FAQ](https://kyrowallet.com/faq/): Answers about Kyro Wallet: is it free, is it custodial, supported blockchains, swap fee, hardware wallets, recovery phrase, Tor, audits, and Windows or macOS warnings.
- [Supported blockchains](https://kyrowallet.com/chains/): Kyro Wallet supports 36 blockchains and 220+ tokens from one recovery phrase: Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB Chain, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base and Avalanche and more. See what works on each.
- [Tor wallet](https://kyrowallet.com/tor/): Kyro is a crypto wallet with Tor built in and on by default: separate circuits per blockchain, no fallback to a direct connection, and a plain list of what each party sees.
- [Monero desktop wallet](https://kyrowallet.com/monero/): A free, open-source Monero desktop wallet for Windows, macOS and Linux. Blocks are scanned on your machine, your view key stays there, and traffic goes over Tor.
- [Swaps](https://kyrowallet.com/swap/): Swap across 33 blockchains with no account. Kyro compares providers, decodes every transaction and includes its fee, from 0.7%, in the rate. Monero included.
- [Earn: staking and lending](https://kyrowallet.com/earn/): Stake SOL, ADA, TRX and NEAR, stake ETH with Lido or lend on Aave from a non-custodial wallet. 14 options, estimated rates and the risks stated plainly.
- [Ledger and Trezor](https://kyrowallet.com/hardware-wallets/): Use a Ledger or Trezor with Kyro on 33 blockchains: one-click connect, Rust decoding, a signature check after signing, and an honest list of limits per chain.
- [Kyro for Windows](https://kyrowallet.com/wallets/windows/): Install Kyro on Windows: one PowerShell command or the 64-bit installer. Free, open source and non-custodial, with built-in Tor. What SmartScreen means, and how updates work.
- [Kyro for macOS](https://kyrowallet.com/wallets/macos/): Install Kyro on your Mac with one Terminal command or the universal .dmg, for Apple Silicon and Intel. Free, open source and non-custodial, with built-in Tor.
- [Kyro for Linux](https://kyrowallet.com/wallets/linux/): Install Kyro on Linux x86_64: one command, an AppImage that updates itself or a .deb. Free, open source and non-custodial, with built-in Tor. FUSE and udev notes.
- [About Kyro](https://kyrowallet.com/about/): Why Kyro exists: a desktop crypto wallet with no account and no analytics, keys on your machine, Tor by default, code anyone can read and a fee anyone can check.
- [Roadmap](https://kyrowallet.com/roadmap/): What Kyro has shipped and what comes next: staking on Polkadot, Sui and Aptos, token sends on more chains, winget and code signing. No dates we cannot keep.
- [Changelog](https://kyrowallet.com/changelog/): What changed in each version of Kyro Wallet, from 1.0.0 to 1.0.7. Generated from the CHANGELOG.md file in the repository.
- [Open source](https://kyrowallet.com/open-source/): Kyro is an open source wallet under GPL-3.0-or-later. How to read the code, build it, verify a release, contribute and report a vulnerability.
- [Brand kit](https://kyrowallet.com/brand/): Download Kyro Wallet logos, marks and app icons, with the colours, typefaces, a short description and simple usage rules for writing about the project.
- [Guides](https://kyrowallet.com/guides/): Plain guides for Kyro Wallet: back up your phrase, verify a download, move from another wallet, swap to Monero, stake SOL and connect a Ledger or Trezor.
- [Glossary](https://kyrowallet.com/glossary/): 39 crypto wallet terms in plain language: recovery phrase, non-custodial, Tor circuit, seed, gas, slippage, staking, blind signing and more.

## Guides

- [First steps with Kyro: set up your wallet](https://kyrowallet.com/guides/first-steps-with-kyro/): Set up Kyro Wallet from scratch: choose a start, set a password, write down your recovery phrase, receive your first coins and send a small test.
- [How to verify your Kyro download with SHA-256](https://kyrowallet.com/guides/verify-your-download/): Check that your Kyro installer is the file published on GitHub Releases: compare its SHA-256 with SHA256SUMS on Windows, macOS or Linux, before you run it.
- [How to back up your recovery phrase safely](https://kyrowallet.com/guides/back-up-your-recovery-phrase/): Your recovery phrase is the only way back into a non-custodial wallet. How to write it down, store it, check it, and what to do if someone sees it.
- [Move to Kyro from another wallet with your phrase](https://kyrowallet.com/guides/move-from-another-wallet/): Import a 12 or 24-word BIP39 recovery phrase into Kyro, or send your coins to a new phrase instead. What carries over, and what can look different.
- [Windows SmartScreen warning for Kyro, explained](https://kyrowallet.com/guides/windows-smartscreen/): Why Windows shows "Windows protected your PC" for Kyro, what it does and does not tell you, how to verify the installer, and how to avoid the warning.
- [Why a crypto wallet should use Tor](https://kyrowallet.com/guides/why-a-wallet-should-use-tor/): Every balance check tells a server your addresses and your IP address. What that leaks, what Tor changes, and what it leaves exposed, in plain words.
- [Address poisoning: how to spot it and stay safe](https://kyrowallet.com/guides/how-to-spot-address-poisoning/): Address poisoning hides a lookalike address in your transaction history so you copy it by mistake. How the scam works, how Kyro flags it, and the habits that stop it.
- [How to swap to Monero (XMR) in your wallet](https://kyrowallet.com/guides/swap-to-monero/): Swap BTC, ETH, SOL, USDT and other coins to XMR inside Kyro, with no account. The steps, what the fee looks like, and what the swap provider can see.
- [How to stake SOL from a desktop wallet](https://kyrowallet.com/guides/stake-sol/): Stake Solana from your own account in Kyro: choose a validator, delegate, wait for activation, then deactivate and withdraw. Risks and timing, without the hype.
- [How to connect a Ledger to Kyro Wallet](https://kyrowallet.com/guides/connect-a-ledger/): Connect a Ledger to Kyro: close Ledger Live, unlock the device, click Connect once and approve each app. Results per chain, blind signing and the limits.
- [How to connect a Trezor to Kyro Wallet](https://kyrowallet.com/guides/connect-a-trezor/): Connect a Trezor to Kyro on desktop: close Trezor Suite, add the device, pair a Safe 7 with its code, and sign with the device. What works, and what does not.
